properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 25 at 5:13AM AKDT until October 25 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 4 and 8
inches, highest amounts from Paxson north.

* WHERE...Northern Copper Valley.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop across the far northern
Copper River Valley beginning early this morning. The heaviest snow
is expected through 4 PM today before slowly tapering off. The best
chance for accumulating snow will be north of mile post 160 with
the highest snow amounts from Paxson north.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 4 and 10
inches.

* WHERE...Northern Susitna Valley.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will continue north of Talkeetna and

into early Monday morning.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 25 at 7:49AM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
There is some dense fog in eastern parts of Williamson and Travis
and western parts of Lee and Bastrop Counties. Visibility in some
places is near 1/4 of a mile. Visibility should increase over the
next couple of hours as temperatures rise. Be careful driving in

you.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 25 at 4:41AM AKDT until October 27 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 3 to 5
feet above the normal high tide line.

* WHERE...Southern Seward Peninsula Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 1 PM AKDT Sunday.
For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM Sunday to 4 AM AKDT
Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Local government officials have reported minor
flooding is occurring along Council Road east of Nome, causing
road damage beyond mile 8, which has caused the closure of the
road beyond that point. Additionally, minor beach erosion is
occurring. For Nome and Golovin, water levels have recently
peaked and will gradually drop into Sunday. While water levels
remain near their apex at this time, in Nome, this can result
in water approaching low-lying homes in Belmont Subdivision
with standing water expected in the port area. For Golovin,
water may inundate any beach property but the roads, buildings
and residences should not be impacted as the water remains
below the berm. Even though water levels drop somewhat, they
will remain normal through early next week. Localized beach
erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...South to southwest winds will continue to
gust up to 40 mph through the weekend. Strong winds continue
into early next week.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 25 at 5:14AM MST until October 26 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the Little Colorado River from earlier
excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Winslow to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until midnight MST tonight /100 AM MDT Monday/.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring near
Birdsprings. Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 513 AM MST /613 AM MDT/, water levels have crested at Winslow
and are expected to continue to fall today. However, downstream
impacts will continue near Birdsprings through the remainder of
the day.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 5:00am MST /6:00am MDT/ the stage was 17.93 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: Water levels will continue to fall through the day,
falling below action stage later this afternoon.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 20 to 25 knots with gusts near 30 knots
and seas 8 to 12 feet through today. Starting tonight, frequent

should subside to Advisory levels once again by Tuesday night.

Reef FL out 20 NM, Waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield
Beach FL from 20 to 60 NM and Waters from Deerfield Beach to

waters of Bahamas.

Gale Warning, from 8 PM this evening to 8 PM EDT Tuesday. A
Small Craft Advisory will then replace the Gale Warning from
midweek onward.

capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for hazardous conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island; Interior Kuskokwim Delta
properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 25 at 3:55AM AKDT until October 26 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 55 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta.

* WHEN...From 4 PM this afternoon to 10 AM AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Southwest winds will build steadily Sunday
morning, becoming strong and gusty by Sunday afternoon. Winds are
expected to be strongest along the coast, but gusts as high as 55
mph are expected to persist inland up to Bethel. Strongest winds
are expected late Sunday night, and winds will begin to diminish
through Monday morning. However, steady southwesterly flow is
expected to continue into midweek.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

NWSheadline: WIND ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 4 PM THIS AFTERNOON TO 10 AM AKDT MONDAY

properties.areaDesc: Mobile Coastal; Baldwin Coastal; Escambia Coastal; Santa Rosa Coastal; Okaloosa Coastal
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 25 at 6:54AM CDT until October 26 at 6:00PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Okaloosa Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH MONDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 25 at 3:52AM AKDT until October 26 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal flooding, with water levels of 2.0 to 3.0 feet
above the normal highest tide line, and 40 mph southwest winds
with gusts up to 55 mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...7 PM Sunday to 7 AM AKDT Monday, highest water levels
expected around midnight Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Kipnuk is expected to see water levels 2.0
to 3.0 ft above the normal high tide line. Kwigillingok and
Kongiganak are expected to have water levels of 1.0 to 2.0 ft
above the normal highest tide line. Following this system,
steady southwesterly flow is expected to continue for the
Kuskokwim Delta coastline through Tuesday, which may slow the
ability for flood waters to recede.
properties.instruction:
A coastal flood advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 7 PM THIS EVENING TO 7 AM AKDT MONDAY
